# Native Coptic-owned Greek NT reference wefts (issue #113)

**Ownership:** both additive weft bundles are generated by **CopticScriptorium-TF**. The `alexsosn/sblgnt` Greek NT repository is a pinned, **read-only** parent. No source change, code, Coptic-specific issue or generated alignment is committed there.

## Schema and trust

From pinned Coptic TT source `CopticScriptorium/corpora@3ac067f1709a0012daf39ea8da2fac79980176a5` and independently pinned Greek NT `alexsosn/sblgnt@4dd0207bda66133fdfa9740ff0aae7de61228700` with exact MorphGNT 6.12 address-space definitions:

| Owner's existing nodes | Native additive node feature | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coptic `sbl_greek`/`sbl_apparatus` | `coptic_nt_ref_id` | Edition-qualified *verse-address candidate* (only if resolved) |
| Same Coptic nodes | `coptic_nt_ref_status` | One of `reference_candidate`, `ambiguous`, `unresolved`, `edition_unavailable`, `unclassified_source` |
| Greek NT parent `verse` nodes | `coptic_nt_ref_id` | Same stable edition-qualified candidate address |
| Same Greek verse nodes | `coptic_nt_source_occurrence_count` | Number of *physical Coptic SBL occurrences* addressing this verse |

These files are sparse native TF **`@node`** features only; no `otype`/`oslots` changes, foreign node IDs as feature values, extra Greek word slots, XML/JSON blobs, cross-language word alignment or corpus text. A physical duplicate in the treebank still counts as its own SBL occurrence, but it does not create a second Greek verse node.

`copticscriptorium_tf.nt_modules` validates source document SHA256, physical occurrence kind/ordinal, exact SBL source attribute, literal Coptic source verse, Coptic parent slot/anchor footprint and actual Greek parent verse section identity. Before projecting, it verifies the **exact Git blob fingerprints** of the read-only Greek parent `otype/oslots/book/chapter/verse` feature files and the known 137,554-word, 7,927-verse warp. Each module embeds cryptographic SHA256 hashes of **both parent warps**, all Greek section-address features, and Coptic `source_record_id`, `source_ordinal`, `value`, `sbl_verse_n`, `source_sha256` and `render_mode`. The Coptic source fingerprints matter: a different SBL Greek string or changed annotation identity can leave `otype/oslots` unchanged. The consumer function `validate_native_module_parent()` checks all those hashes before loading a weft, and the real-data pilot deliberately calls it for both projections.

Publication is atomic no-overwrite. Both projections' reference/count multisets must be identical before any files are published; the writer rejects a target that exists, unknown fields/statuses, forged editions, invalid node identifiers, missing candidate statuses, and mismatched counts.

## Research → RED → actual native TF tests

The original 2,628-record audit has **2,301** address candidates, **437** ambiguous, **8** unresolved and **1** source-proven `edition_unavailable` annotations across 48 physical annotated TT records. The native module writer/projection TDD covers fake node IDs, wrong target parent verse, incorrect source literals, duplicate/extra Coptic native annotations, altered parent fingerprints, empty or inconsistent modules and atomic no-clobber publication.

The exact-pinned real-data CI pilot converts **only three source TT records** (Mark 2, 1 Corinthians 2, independent treebank Mark 2), reloads their native Coptic TF plus the unchanged historical Greek NT TF, projects weft features to existing Coptic SBL nodes and Greek verse nodes, reloads each side with its module, and verifies the candidate-count crosswalk. The heavy 2.394M-slot full native TF build is deliberately **not** repeated on each weft-code PR; full-corpus projection and consumer qualification remain a separate integration/release gate.

## How this differs from alignment

This is **source-supported verse address interoperability**, not word alignment, Greek text equality, a translation equivalence assertion or a replacement for the Greek textual apparatus. Historical Coptic `Greek_source` provenance references the 2010 SBLGNT and cannot certify reading identity with the 2024 MorphGNT parent. John 7:53–8:11 has no morphological parent verse in pinned MorphGNT. Remaining suspicious source annotations (notably Mark 1) are independently researched in [issue #117](https://github.com/alexsosn/CopticScriptorium-TF/issues/117), and they remain ambiguous until resolved with source evidence.

No generated Greek or restricted Coptic corpus is released by this work.
